Continuous distal outcome means by class (BCH; Mplus AUXILIARY = y (BCH))

bch.Rd

Class-specific means of a continuous distal outcome by the bias-adjusted three-step method of Bolck, Croon & Hagenaars (2004) in the form of Vermunt (2010), as Mplus AUXILIARY = y (BCH), with Wald tests of equal means across classes.

Usage

bch(object, data, y, name = NULL, wave = NULL, waves = NULL)

Arguments

object

A fitted latentmix model (K >= 2).

data

Data frame with one row per row of the data the model was fitted to, or (backward compatible) the numeric outcome vector itself with y omitted.

y

Outcome column of data (tidyselect, one numeric column), e.g. income.

name

Label of the outcome in output (default: the column name, else "y").

wave, waves

For an LTA: means by the class at one wave (wave, default the last) or by the class pattern at several waves (waves = c(2, 3); patterns ordered with the last wave changing fastest). The BCH weights are those of the K^T class paths, as Mplus saves them (SAVE = BCHWEIGHTS) for models with several latent class variables.

Value

An object of class c("latentmix_bch", "latentmix_aux"), a list with name, means, se (standard errors of the means) and variances (one per class), overall (list with chisq, df, p of the overall Wald test), pairwise (data frame of pairwise Wald tests with classes a, b, chisq, p), n (rows used), ndeleted (rows with missing outcome) and text.

Details

Each analysed row is weighted, for every class, by the inverse of the classification error matrix of the measurement model (BCH weights), so the measurement model is kept fixed and the outcome does not shift the classes. BCH weights can be negative, so a within-class variance can occasionally be negative: the means and their standard errors remain valid (Julia then warns). Sampling weights and the survey design (cluster, strata) of the model are used. Rows with a missing outcome are excluded. data must have one row per row of the data the model was fitted to, in the same order. BCH is robust to unequal outcome variances across classes (Bakk & Vermunt 2016).

References

Bolck, A., Croon, M., & Hagenaars, J. (2004). Estimating latent structure models with categorical variables: One-step versus three-step estimators. Political Analysis, 12(1), 3–27. doi:10.1093/pan/mph001

Vermunt, J. K. (2010). Latent class modeling with covariates: Two improved three-step approaches. Political Analysis, 18(4), 450–469. doi:10.1093/pan/mpq025

Bakk, Z., & Vermunt, J. K. (2016). Robustness of stepwise latent class modeling with continuous distal outcomes. Structural Equation Modeling, 23(1), 20–31. doi:10.1080/10705511.2014.955104

Asparouhov, T., & Muthén, B. (2014). Auxiliary variables in mixture modeling: Three-step approaches using Mplus. Structural Equation Modeling, 21(3), 329–341. doi:10.1080/10705511.2014.915181

See also

dcat() for categorical outcomes, r3step(), lm_table() (several outcomes side by side).

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
# Do the ACE classes differ in adult depressive symptoms (depress, 0-24)?
m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)     # 4 ACE classes, as generated
#> Starting Julia ...
b <- bch(m, aces, depress)
b   # class means with SEs and Wald tests; generated means 4 (Low) to 13 (High adversity)
#> ━━ BCH: distal outcome depress by class ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#>   n = 1453 (47 rows with missing outcome excluded)
#> 
#>   ──────────────────────────────
#>   Class    Mean     SE  Variance
#>   ──────────────────────────────
#>   1       4.761  0.138    12.101
#>   2      10.259  0.297    12.933
#>   3       6.985  0.320     7.295
#>   4      13.800  0.436    12.509
#>   ──────────────────────────────
#> 
#> ── Wald tests of equal means ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────
#>   Test           Chi-square  df       p
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────
#>   Overall           647.903   3  <0.001
#>   Class 1 vs. 2     264.856   1  <0.001
#>   Class 1 vs. 3      36.417   1  <0.001
#>   Class 1 vs. 4     392.358   1  <0.001
#>   Class 2 vs. 3      51.610   1  <0.001
#>   Class 2 vs. 4      39.751   1  <0.001
#>   Class 3 vs. 4     143.693   1  <0.001
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────
# smoking (0/1): its BCH "mean" is the proportion of smokers in each class
lm_table(b, bch(m, aces, smoker), format = "markdown")
#> **Distal outcome means by latent class (BCH)**
#> 
#> | Class | depress | smoker |
#> | :--- | ---: | ---: |
#> | Class 1 | 4.761 (0.138) | 0.155 (0.014) |
#> | Class 2 | 10.259 (0.297) | 0.266 (0.033) |
#> | Class 3 | 6.985 (0.320) | 0.249 (0.039) |
#> | Class 4 | 13.800 (0.436) | 0.440 (0.050) |
#> 
#> *Means with robust standard errors in parentheses.*  
#> *depress: Overall Wald test: χ²(3) = 647.90, p < 0.001. n = 1453.*  
#> *smoker: Overall Wald test: χ²(3) = 43.99, p < 0.001. n = 1500.*  
# }
